document.title: Finally, A Talkative Talib: Origins and Membership of the Religious Students' Movement
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Based on a Talib source, offers an in-depth sketch of Mullah Mohammed Omar and the creation and organization of the Taliban. The source denies foreign patronage and says the movement disliked Saudi interference and ISI efforts to treat Afghanistan like another province. Also raises the expiring Durand Accord and Pashtunistan.

events.description: Summer 1994: Kandahar deteriorates; madrasa students gang-raped by local commander; Omar relates vision to Haji Bashar.
Haji Bashar raises 8 million Pakistani rupees and six pick-up trucks for the Taliban.
Taliban seize Spin Boldak and its armory from Hekmatyar commander; later stop and then escort Pakistan's Central Asian convoy across Kandahar.
Embassy political officer contacted by an intermediary offering a meeting with a Taliban insider.
Embassy political officer meets Taliban insider.
Haji Bashar due back from Umra; secret meeting with UN/US proposed.
Poloff contacted by source who claimed a friend in senior Taliban leadership.
Poloff met with Taliban insider and a translator.
Summer 1994: several madrasa students gang-raped by a local commander in Kandahar; Omar relates vision to Haji Bashar, who raises funds.
Taliban take over Meiwand district administration, then seize Spin Boldak and its armory.
Taliban stop Pakistani Central Asian convoy of 30 trucks at Boldak, then agree to escort it across Kandahar and cut chains laid by commanders.
Taliban insider describes the High Council of eight and 22-member shura structure to US Embassy officials.
Hizb-i-Wahdat in Kabul begins negotiations with the Taliban.
Source accompanied representatives of Khalis, Sayyaf and Mohemmadi to Kandahar, where they pledged support to the Taliban.
Dostam sends emissaries to the Taliban promising to surrender under conditions.
Abdul-Samad assembles 30 ulema in Maroof who issue a public statement against growing and trading narcotics; farmers warned of Shariah punishment.
Haji Bashar due to return from performing Umra, after which a secret meeting with the UN could be arranged.

sources_cited: Confidential interview of a Taliban insider by U.S. Embassy Islamabad political officer, 17 Feb 1995
key_claims: A Taliban insider claims the movement is not supported by foreign governments but has links to Pashtuns in Pakistan and conservative religious parties via madrasas.
The Taliban began in Meiwand at Haji Bashar's madrasa, with Mohammed Omar, a one-eyed Hotak ex-Khalis fighter, as leader.
Haji Bashar financed the early movement with 8 million rupees and six pickup trucks.
The Taliban denied Pakistani Frontier Corps backing in seizing the Spin Boldak armory and said Babar had not consulted them over the convoy.
Structure: eight-member High Council led by Omar, Bashar and Hassan, plus a 22-member shura; Mullah Borjan is military commander.
Taliban resent Saudi and ISI/Pakistani interference and want good relations with the US and UN.
Several rival commanders reportedly approached or pledged support to the Taliban.
